questions.question: What is a Docker image?
options: A read only template used to create containers
questions.explanation: An image is an immutable layered filesystem plus metadata. A container is a running instance of it.

questions.question: Which instruction in a Dockerfile sets the command run when the container starts?
questions.explanation: CMD (or ENTRYPOINT) defines the start command. RUN executes during the build.

questions.question: What does docker ps show by default?
questions.explanation: docker ps lists running containers; -a adds stopped ones.

questions.question: Why put COPY package.json before COPY . in a Node Dockerfile?
options: Dependencies are cached in their own layer and reinstall only when the manifest changes
questions.explanation: Layer caching keys on the copied files, so copying the manifest first keeps the install layer valid across code changes.

questions.question: What is the difference between a volume and a bind mount?
options: A volume is managed by Docker, a bind mount maps a specific host path
Bind mounts survive container deletion, volumes do not
questions.explanation: Volumes live in Docker's storage area and are portable; bind mounts point at an exact host directory.

questions.question: What does EXPOSE actually do?
options: Publishes the port on the host
Documents the port and informs tooling, without publishing it
questions.explanation: EXPOSE is metadata. Publishing requires -p or a ports entry in Compose.

questions.question: Why is a multi stage build useful?
options: Build tools stay in an earlier stage so the final image ships only the artefacts
It allows multiple base images at runtime
questions.explanation: You compile in a heavy stage and copy only the output into a slim final stage, cutting image size and attack surface.

questions.question: What happens to data written inside a container's writable layer when it is removed?
options: It is lost unless a volume or bind mount was used
It stays in the build cache
questions.explanation: The writable layer is deleted with the container, which is why stateful paths need volumes.

questions.question: Why does each RUN instruction matter for image size?
options: Every RUN creates a layer, so files deleted in a later layer still occupy space
questions.explanation: Layers are additive, so cleanup must happen in the same RUN that created the files.
